messages:
morgan: Heads up — during yesterday's canary we saw a weird "slow start" for streaming responses. p95 for full-stream looks ok but first-token p99 spikes ~180ms on a subset of requests. attaching traces in next msg.

liam: thanks. is this correlated with the kernel selector change we merged? not sure why first token only would jump.

anya: perf-bot trace shows a KV cache miss pattern on the first few microbatches. when kv-miss we do backend lookup + populate which adds ~30-60ms depending on seq len.

perf-bot: automated-trace: trace_id=tr-20260301-7f2b
span[0] root -> 5ms
span[1] kernel-selection -> 3ms
span[2] kv-lookup (miss) -> 42ms
span[3] emit-first-chunk -> 2ms
note: 38% of p99 cases have kv-lookup miss on first token.

devon: that matches the telemetry I saw: sessions with fresh KV state have a larger first-token latency. after a few tokens, KV warmup amortizes and tail collapses.

sasha: two levers we discussed: 1) smaller initial flush interval (send tiny chunk immediately), 2) aggressive prefetch/warm on session start. both have tradeoffs.

liam: smaller flush interval reduces perceived latency but increases overall request count and can harm throughput. we need numbers. can we quantify cost delta for fast-first-chunk=20ms vs 40ms?

anya: ran microbench yesterday — summary:
- baseline flush_interval=40ms: first-token p99=175ms, tokens/sec=1050
- fast-first flush_interval=20ms: first-token p99=95ms, tokens/sec=980 (-6.7%)
- prefill+warm (async kv preload): first-token p99=85ms, tokens/sec=1020 (-2.8%)
notes: prefill requires extra DB calls up front but amortized if session uses >8 tokens.

morgan: useful. kernel-selection is adding 3-6ms only, so root cause is KV miss + flush timing. any perf regressions from the kernel change are negligible compared to kv latency.

devon: one more datapoint: when microbatch size is larger (N=24) we get slightly better throughput but worse first-token p95/p99 since batching waits for more inflight tokens. so microbatch sizing interacts with flush interval.

sasha: proposal: implement "fast-first-chunk" feature flag — for the first chunk only, use flush_interval=15ms and force an async kv-prefetch if no cached entry. fallback to normal behavior after chunk 1. A/B canary at 5% for 24h.

liam: +1. add metric: first_token_latency.p50/p95/p99 and cost_per_token difference and requests/sec. Also track kv-prefetch error rate.

anya: I'll drop the canary config and perf dashboard. quick config snippet: 
```yaml
feature_flags:
  fast_first_chunk: true
  fast_first_chunk_interval_ms: 15
  kv_prefetch_on_start: async
  kv_prefetch_timeout_ms: 50
```

morgan: roll plan: canary 5% -> monitor 4h + commit if p99 first_token reduces w/o >3% tokens/sec regression. owners: anya (perf config), sasha (runtime flag), devon (kv infra).

devon: note: implement a lightweight in-memory prefetch layer to avoid DB storms. prefetch should be best-effort and backoff on errors.

liam: also add tracing tag kernel_variant so we can separate cases where kernel selection path differs. helps isolate tiny 3-6ms deltas.

anya: created dashboard: rows for first_token_latency (by kernel_variant, by kv_hit/miss), tokens/sec, cpu/gpu utilization, kv_miss_rate. will post link after I finish.

morgan: thanks team. if the canary shows success we'll roll to 20% and consider defaulting fast-first for interactive workloads. otherwise revert and iterate on prefetch. :thumbsup:
